newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan DECEMBER M2 money supply up 7.95 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan DECEMBER M2 money supply up 7.95 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 7.95 percent in December from a year earlier, bringing the full-year 1996 rise to 8.12 percent compared to 1995, the central bank said in a statement on Saturday.
The December rise, the lowest increase April, was well below the central bank's monthly target of 9-14 percent.
The bank attributed the below-target rise to slow investment growth in December.
"(The low rise) was caused by a clear slowdown in bank loans and investment growth," it said in a statement.
A Reuters poll of Taiwan economists conducted on January 21 had yielded an average forecast of an 8.30-percent rise for the December M2 growth.
Analysts said the lower-than-expected growth meant overall demand for money was not strong, reflecting a frustratingly slow economic recovery.

"The low growth means the economy still was not in a vibrant state in December, that it may be a couple more months before a clear recovery is seen," said Michael Hung, an economist at Nikko Securities.
